items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Lloyd Wilson, who was a trumpet player from Detroit, he and his wife shared a house with us... My husband and I had a little house and we shared this house with another musician, Lloyd Wilson, and his wife. He was a trumpet player. He worked here. He used to work at a place called Papke's.

ctx.x: I've never heard of it before.

Papke's. It was called Papke's. And this guy, anyway, he got to know a lot of musicians, Lloyd did, Lloyd Wilson, he got to know an awful lot of musicians. He did know a lot of musicians because he was from Texas, but he had lived back east quite awhile, and particularly in Detroit. He lived in Detroit. So he used to meet the musicians when they'd come to town, you know, and they'd bring them to our house, you know. And they'd come to our house, he'd bring them over and he wasn't what you'd call a great trumpet…

was not. But he was a nice guy, very personable, and all the guys just loved Lloyd Wilson, and he used to bring these guys to the house, and we would jam. That's what we used to do, have jam sessions at my house, you know. And I got the chance to meet so many marvelous musicians at that particular time. Eddie Barefield was one guy that I met. I met Panama Francis in those years, years ago. I met -- I met -- well, I think Benny, I think I met Benny Carter, if I'm thinking correctly, at that time. Anyway, they all…
